sections.text:
The song was written by Brown and his songwriting team, the Graffiti Artists (Rob Allen and Andre Merritt). He stated that after entering the studio, Polow da Don created a beat that Brown wrote along to. Because the producer's style was "more of a European, techno, house-type feel," the group "wanted to give it that other side of crossover, and go a little bit to that pop realm". "Forever" is one of four new songs Brown recorded for the re-release of his second studio album Exclusive. The song was first intended to be on Brown's following album, but decided he "wasn't ready to release a new album yet".

"Forever" is an extended version of a commercial jingle for Doublemint gum, commissioned by an advertising company working for Wrigley. Brown first created the short version for the commercial, then extended and expanded it into a full song during a recording session in February 2007, which was paid for by the gum company. Originally, the plan was to follow up his third single, "With You", with the Kanye West-featuring "Down", but the new material won out. Although the label initially was reluctant to release "Forever" as a single, the song was so "potent and strong" that it overruled any hesitations regarding its commercial connections.

The song was first released for digital download on November 2, 2007, in Denmark, Belgium, and New Zealand, and on November 6 in France. The next year, it was released on April 22, 2008, in Australia, Canada, and Japan, then on August 12, 2008, in the United States and Germany.

An EP featuring three remixes was released in Ireland on June 13, 2008, in Australia, Austria and the Netherlands on June 16, 2008, and in Japan on August 13, 2008.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: "Forever" is a [[dance-pop]]<ref name=nytimes>{{cite news|last=Ratliff|first=Ben|title=Nary a Carol in Earshot, and a Santa in Heels|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/12/15/arts/music/15jing.html|work=New York Times|date=14 December 2008 |access-date=19 February 2012}}</ref> [[love song]] that runs for 4 minutes and 38 seconds.<ref name="bbreview"/> It contains influences of [[Trance music|trance]] and [[techno]],<ref name="About.com"/> as well as of [[Timbaland]]'s production style, with synthesized voices over a drum machine pattern.<ref name="About.com"/> Brown performed the song using the [[autotune]] vocal effect, as he did in one of his previous singles, "[[Kiss Kiss (Chris Brown song)|Kiss Kiss]]".<ref>[http://www.newyorker.com/arts/critics/musical/2008/06/09/080609crmu_music_frerejones?currentPage=all The Gerbil's Revenge: Musical Events: The New Yorker] Accessed July 23, 2008</ref> According to the digital sheet music published at Musicnotes.com by [[EMI Music Publishing]], it is written in the key of [[B major]], with a simple chord progression of E-B-F♯-C♯m. The song maintains a tempo of 120 beats per minute in common time. Brown's vocal range spans nearly an octave and a half from B3 to G♯5.<ref name="Musicnotes">{{cite journal|title=Digital Sheet Music – Rihanna – Break It Off|publisher= [[Sony/ATV Music Publishing]]}}</ref>
sections.text: "Forever" is a dance-pop love song that runs for 4 minutes and 38 seconds. It contains influences of trance and techno, as well as of Timbaland's production style, with synthesized voices over a drum machine pattern. Brown performed the song using the autotune vocal effect, as he did in one of his previous singles, "Kiss Kiss". According to the digital sheet music published at Musicnotes.com by EMI Music Publishing, it is written in the key of B major, with a simple chord progression of E-B-F♯-C♯m. The song maintains a tempo of 120 beats per minute in common time. Brown's vocal range spans nearly an octave and a half from B3 to G♯5.

sections.heading: Background and synopsis
sections.wikitext:
The two-day shoot took place in [[Los Angeles, California]], at the beginning of March 2008. It was directed by [[Joseph Kahn (director)|Joseph Kahn]]. The video premiered on ''[[Total Request Live|TRL]]'' on April 30, 2008, and on [[Black Entertainment Television|BET]]'s ''[[106 & Park]]'' on May 5, 2008. The video reached number one on the MTV Online Chart.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071118005824/http://www.mtv.co.uk/channel/mtvbase/video MTV Base] MTV UK. Accessed May 11, 2008.</ref> BET placed the song at number 55 on their ''Notarized: Top 100 Videos'' countdown. Brown's main love interest in the video is played by model Megan Abrigo.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.myspace.com/meganabrigo |title=Megan Abrigo (The Official Megan Abrigo Myspace Page) on Myspace |publisher=Myspace.com}}</ref>

The [[music video]] starts off with Brown driving up to a [[nightclub]], unwrapping a fresh stick of Doublemint gum, and walking inside. People are seen dancing while Brown starts to sing the first verse. Brown is also seen singing with light effects circling him. During the choruses, Brown and his background dancers start to [[house dance]] on the empty dance floor. Among the dancers are [[Marie Courchinoux]] and [[Rino Nakasone Razalan]] from [[Beat Freaks]]. In the second verse, Brown is walking outside the club following his love interest. Later he is seen performing a [[540 Kick|540 crescent kick]] in front of a water fountain. During the bridge, Brown is seen in the top roof with his love interest; the girl falls off the roof and Brown jumps to catch her. The two land safely, and after the final chorus, Brown drives away from the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5sMKX22BHeE|title=Chris Brown - Forever|work=[[YouTube]]|date=October 25, 2009|access-date=January 31, 2018}}</ref>

The video premiered on TRL on April 30, 2008, and on BET's 106 & Park on May 5, 2008. The video reached number one on the MTV Online Chart. BET placed the song at number 55 on their Notarized: Top 100 Videos countdown. Brown's main love interest in the video is played by model Megan Abrigo.

The music video starts off with Brown driving up to a nightclub, unwrapping a fresh stick of Doublemint gum, and walking inside. People are seen dancing while Brown starts to sing the first verse. Brown is also seen singing with light effects circling him. During the choruses, Brown and his background dancers start to house dance on the empty dance floor. Among the dancers are Marie Courchinoux and Rino Nakasone Razalan from Beat Freaks. In the second verse, Brown is walking outside the club following his love interest. Later he is seen performing a 540 crescent kick in front of a water fountain. During the bridge, Brown is seen in the top roof with his love interest; the girl falls off the roof and Brown jumps to catch her. The two land safely, and after the final chorus, Brown drives away from the club.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
According to the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'', the song's video is "digital dream about sharing with one who makes your world stop."<ref name="bbreview" /> The video was popular in American television. The video for "Forever" debuted on BET's ''106 & Park'' at number 10 on July 21, 2008, before finally reach number 2 and has stayed in the countdown for nine days. The video also has reached number 2 on for 8 days [[MTV]] ''[[Total Request Live|TRL]]'' and has stayed in the countdown for 29 days.

The video for "Forever" was also popular enough across Asia, by debuting at number 13 on [[MTV Asia]] program, "Chart Attack", which count 20 most popular video in [[Asia]] and so far has peaked at number 1 replacing [[Mariah Carey]]'s "[[Bye Bye (Mariah Carey song)|Bye Bye]]". "Forever" also debuted at number 7 on MTV Hip Hop Countdown; MTV Asian program which count 10 most popular [[urban contemporary|urban]] video in the region and has reached number 1 for six consecutive weeks.<ref>[http://www.mtvasia.com/Onair/Shows/HipHopCountdown/ MTV Hip Hop Countdown Chart] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080704093814/http://www.mtvasia.com/Onair/Shows/HipHopCountdown/ |date=2008-07-04 }} ''MTV Asia''. Accessed July 3, 2008.</ref> In UK, it has reached number 1 on MTV Base. It also has peaked at number 1 on the MTV Online Chart for several weeks.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071118005824/http://www.mtv.co.uk/channel/mtvbase/video MTV Base] ''MTV UK''. Accessed April 17, 2008.</ref> The video was nominated in the "Best Dancing in a Video", "Best Choreography" and "Video of the Year" categories [[2008 MTV Video Music Awards]].

sections.wikitext: Bill Lamb of [[About.com]] gave the song four and a half stars, and said it was one of Brown's best to date.<ref name="About.com">[http://top40.about.com/od/singles/gr/chrisbrownfor.htm Chris Brown - "Forever"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924052804/http://top40.about.com/od/singles/gr/chrisbrownfor.htm |date=2015-09-24 }} About.com. Accessed June 19, 2008.</ref> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' stated that the single "is really a love song but bangs with electrified production from Polow Da Don to ignite dancefloors."<ref name="bbreview">Menachem, Michael. [https://web.archive.org/web/20081227035731/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/content_display/reviews/singles/e3id5f52df31901946cc6e2d5c411bfe19f Single Reviews: Forever]. ''Billboard''. sections.text: Bill Lamb of About.com gave the song four and a half stars, and said it was one of Brown's best to date. Billboard stated that the single "is really a love song but bangs with electrified production from Polow Da Don to ignite dancefloors." Alex Fletcher of Digital Spy gave the song two out of five stars, saying "Listening to 'Forever' is a pleasant enough experience, but this track never truly sparks into life or finds its own identity." He went on to say that, "His style is a bit hard to distinguish from Usher, Ne-Yo and the rest of the current crop of American male solo artists." HotNewHipHop mentioned "Forever" as a "standout track in Chris Brown’s discography, highlighting his ability to craft timeless hits that transcend musical genres".

In other media
sections.wikitext:
* On July 16, 2008, Comfort Fedoke and Stephen "Twitch" Boss from the US television [[reality program]] and dance competition ''[[So You Think You Can Dance (Season 4)|So You Think You Can Dance]]'' danced to "Forever" as the part of the competition.<ref>{{cite web|last=Williams|first=John-John|date=August 8, 2008|title='So You Think You Can Dance': finale details|work=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2008/08/08/so-you-think-you-can-dance-finale-details/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081227045001/http://weblogs.baltimoresun.com/entertainment/realitycheck/blog/2008/08/so_you_think_you_can_dance_4.html|url-status=live|archive-date=December 27, 2008|access-date=November 22, 2008}}</ref> [[Quest Crew]] and SoReal Cru danced to this song on ''[[America's Best Dance Crew]]''.
* In 2009 American [[parody]] comedy movie ''[[Dance Flick]]'', the song was used in a scene where the protagonist is in a club, and when ''Forever'' comes up he screams "This is my song!" and he starts dancing.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_9pYHx65is|title=YouTube|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref>
* On July 19, 2009, a video was uploaded on [[YouTube]] that received significant media attention, using "Forever" as the song to a [[wedding march]]. The video, known as the [[JK Wedding Entrance Dance]] video, received over 1.7 million views in its first seven days.<ref>{{cite web|last=Santo |first=Michael |url=http://www.huliq.com/3257/84023/jk-wedding-entrance-dance-becomes-youtube-sensation |title=JK Wedding Entrance Dance Becomes YouTube Sensation |publisher=HULIQ |date=July 24, 2009 |access-date=November 26, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.canada.com/Unusual+wedding+video+viral/1828664/story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090728035523/http://www.canada.com/Unusual+wedding+video+viral/1828664/story.html |archive-date=July 28, 2009 |title=Unusual wedding video is a viral hit}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.nydailynews.com/news/2009/07/24/2009-07-24_fun_minnesota_couple_jill_peterson_and_kevin_heinz_dance_down_the_aisle_at_their.html |location=New York |work=Daily News |title=Fun Minnesota couple Jill Peterson and Kevin Heinz dance down the aisle at their wedding |first=Kate |last=Nocera |date=July 29, 2009}}</ref> The popularity of the video caused a resurgence of the song, landing it back into the top ten singles on [[iTunes]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.yahoo.com/s/nm/20090729/music_nm/us_brown_2 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090802002207/http://news.yahoo.com/s/nm/20090729/music_nm/us_brown_2 |archive-date=August 2, 2009 |title=Viral wedding video gives Brown's "Forever" a boost}}</ref> By July 4, 2023, the video had received 105,101,387 hits. Due to the circumstances surrounding the song in their wedding video (the Chris Brown/Rihanna incident), on their website, the couple in the video asked that donations be made to a [[domestic violence]] charity.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jkweddingdance.com/ |title=Jill and Kevin wedding |work=Jkweddingdance.com |access-date=November 26, 2011}}</ref>
* On October 8, 2009, "Forever" was used in the American version of ''[[The Office (U.S. TV series)|The Office]]'' at [[Jim Halpert|Jim]] and [[Pam Beesly|Pam's]] [[Niagara (The Office)|wedding]] as part of an homage of the aforementioned JK Wedding. Again, it caused the song to move back into the top twenty singles on [[iTunes]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2010 it was used in another JK Wedding homage, in the Irish TV series ''[[Love/Hate (TV series)|Love/Hate]]''.
* On March 30, 2010, [[Andrew Garcia]] performed an acoustic cover of the song on the top 10 performance night of ''American Idol''. He chose this as his R&B song selection. His non-acoustic full-length recording of the song was released on the iTunes Store as "Forever (American Idol Studio Version) – Single" during the season's run and was later included as part of the ''American Idol Season 9'' album that featured the top 10 finalists.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}}
* On January 13, 2012, this song, along with "[[I Want to Take You Higher]]" by [[Sly & the Family Stone]], [[Yeah! (Usher song)|"Yeah!"]] by [[Usher (singer)|Usher]] and [[Signed, Sealed, Delivered I'm Yours|"Signed, Sealed, Delivered, I'm Yours"]] by [[Stevie Wonder]], was featured in the film ''[[Joyful Noise (film)|Joyful Noise]]'' with [[Dolly Parton]], Angela Grovey, and [[DeQuina Moore]] singing a part of it in the "Higher Medley".

The popularity of the video caused a resurgence of the song, landing it back into the top ten singles on iTunes. By July 4, 2023, the video had received 105,101,387 hits. Due to the circumstances surrounding the song in their wedding video (the Chris Brown/Rihanna incident), on their website, the couple in the video asked that donations be made to a domestic violence charity.

Again, it caused the song to move back into the top twenty singles on iTunes.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}} In 2010 it was used in another JK Wedding homage, in the Irish TV series Love/Hate.
* On March 30, 2010, Andrew Garcia performed an acoustic cover of the song on the top 10 performance night of American Idol. He chose this as his R&B song selection. His non-acoustic full-length recording of the song was released on the iTunes Store as "Forever (American Idol Studio Version) – Single" during the season's run and was later included as part of the American Idol Season 9 album that featured the top 10 finalists.{{Citation needed|date=October 2021}}
* On January 13, 2012, this song, along with "I Want to Take You Higher" by Sly & the Family Stone, "Yeah!" by Usher and "Signed, Sealed, Delivered, I'm Yours" by Stevie Wonder, was featured in the film Joyful Noise with Dolly Parton, Angela Grovey, and DeQuina Moore singing a part of it in the "Higher Medley".
